name: CISC-16
description: RISC-16's opposite: every arithmetic instruction can reach memory, through eight addressing modes written the way real assemblers write them (ADD R0, [R6 - 1] is R0 = R0 + [R6 - 1]), one instruction copies memory to memory, and ENTER and LEAVE build stack frames for recursion.
tagline: Eight addressing modes, written in brackets

programs.name: Sum a table
programs.description: Immediate, absolute and post-increment operands: ADD R0, [R1]+ adds the next cell and steps on

programs.name: Copy a string
programs.description: MOV [R2]+, [R1]+ copies a character memory to memory and steps both pointers: a loop body in one instruction

programs.name: Recursive Fibonacci
programs.description: fib(n) calls itself twice; ENTER, LEAVE and an indexed local keep every call's values in its own stack frame

programs.name: Code is data
programs.description: The program rewrites its own instructions: ADD [R1 + 1], 1 changes the letter OUT 'A' prints, and MOV [start], [stop] copies a HLT over the first instruction

programs.name: Reverse a word
programs.description: Register plus register, [R1 + R3], walks the word, [PC + length] reads a number stored after the code, and BRA loops by a distance instead of an address
